ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: The left side of the figure shows a Br3C—Br structure, namely a central carbon connected to three bromines and also bonded to another bromine; the right side shows a :PPh3 with a lone-pair marking, with no ordinary covalent bond to the left structure. There are also curved arrows in the figure, but the problem asks to ignore these arrows. Reasoning: After ignoring the arrows, the left species is a carbon tetrabromide fragment in which carbon is connected to four bromines, and the SMILES can be written as BrC(Br)(Br)Br. The right :PPh3 is triphenylphosphine, and the SMILES according to the specified writing is c1ccc(P(c2ccccc2)c2ccccc2)cc1. The two species are disconnected from each other, so connect the two SMILES with '.'.

raw_record.question_text: What is the SMILES expression of the transition-state structure shown in the image, ignoring the arrows?

method.method_draft: First describe the visual structure: identify two disconnected chemical species, Br3C—Br and :PPh3, while excluding all curved arrows. Convert Br3C—Br to the SMILES for carbon bonded to four bromines, BrC(Br)(Br)Br. Convert PPh3 to triphenylphosphine by attaching three phenyl rings to phosphorus, c1ccc(P(c2ccccc2)c2ccccc2)cc1. Join the two disconnected molecules with '.', yielding BrC(Br)(Br)Br.c1ccc(P(c2ccccc2)c2ccccc2)cc1.
